speaker: karunapadiachi
text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. So the Black Cat device has been used by a few municipalities within the area, within the county, well, close to two years now. It's a fairly effective device. We had an older version of the speed measuring equipment and that, unfortunately, we had to retire due to age. The new device, which we were able to get on loan from the company as a trial, we deployed it a couple of times around the county. It's fairly effective, it allows us to monitor speeds, record speeds of vehicles going in both directions. It also has a software program that allows us to analyze the data so we can ascertain peak periods when speeding may be an issue. That is really effective for us when it comes to providing policing services. So as opposed to a speeding complaint, we would normally get a speeding complaint. There's a vehicle on Roger Stevens Road, or vehicles are speeding on Roger Stevens Road, and there's no real time, and we really can't deploy a cruiser there for 24 hours a day, seven days a week. That's just not realistic. What this device allows us to do is monitor the vehicle traffic, the speeds, ascertain a period of time where volume is heavy or speeds are the greatest, and then we can deploy our resources accordingly. So we've worked with a couple of the local municipalities who already have it in their possession, and use their machine to get some data, and it's been really effective. What I can also tell you is it not only goes towards policing and speed enforcement, but also some of the municipalities provide it to their roads people so they can do traffic studies and so forth. text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. So as everyone is aware, the convoy arrived in Ottawa just near the beginning of February. Ottawa police requested OPP assistance in the days and weeks thereafter.
